text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Conservative opposition leader Mesut Yilmaz says government aims to silence press by planned new restrictions.
- Turkey to post special police force in airports.
- A parliamentary sub-commission investigating contract irregularities at the TEDAS electricity company says then prime minister Tansu Ciller should face the Supreme Court.
- Turkey's top policeman vows that alleged links between organised crime, police and the state will not be covered up.
- Tourism ministry will monitor the hotels in Istanbul's Laleli district where 17 people died in a hotel fire on Sunday.
- Former far-right activist says he was part of a state-backed hit team that killed an Armenian guerrilla leader in Athens in 1988.
- A Turk killed by Greek coastguard vessel.
- Privatisation Board sues dairy products company Mis Sut, for violating the sales contract by closing down three plants.
- Turkey is caught in the web of gambling. It boasts 40 five-star casinos.
- The husband of junior coalition leader Tansu Ciller is alleged to be behind government's plans to clamp down on media.
